title: The One With Chandler And Monicas Wedding

jokes.text: What's happening to the coffeehouse?
jokes.setup: Ross says this is the last time they'll be here as six single people, implying a major life change
jokes.punchline: Joey mishears the emotional statement and panics about the coffeehouse itself closing, revealing his priorities
jokes.explanation: Classic Joey misunderstanding that is perfectly in character. His panic about the coffee shop rather than the wedding is a tight, economical joke that gets a lot done in four words.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: She's my wife, my better half, my significant other.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: My ball and chain, my old lady, my squaw.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: My property, my chattel, my... my reason for living but also the source of all my problems.

jokes.text: From now on, it's you four and me and the missus. The little woman. The wife. The old ball and chain.
jokes.setup: Chandler is describing his impending marriage using old-fashioned, sexist idioms
jokes.punchline: He lists increasingly dated/negative nicknames for a wife, undermining his own enthusiasm for the wedding
jokes.explanation: Functional Chandler self-deprecating humor. The escalating list of negative wife-nicknames is a mild gag, but the punchline is predictable.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm not old!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: You're right, you're not old. You're... seasoned.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's not better!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Okay, okay. You're a beautiful, intelligent, sophisticated woman who just happens to have been around since the dinosaurs.

jokes.text: Old? / The young, hot ball and chain. / Much better.
jokes.setup: Chandler calls Monica 'the old ball and chain'
jokes.punchline: Monica's one-word protest causes instant overcorrection to 'young, hot' — revealing who holds the power in the relationship
jokes.explanation: Very economical exchange. Monica's single-word correction and Chandler's instant capitulation is a compact, well-structured bit about their dynamic.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Did you say lunch?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm in!

jokes.text: Joey, you too? / I just heard 'lunch.'
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel are heading out for the dress and lunch with mom — an errand not meant for Joey
jokes.punchline: Joey admits he's only joining because he heard the word 'lunch,' stripping away any pretense of social awareness
jokes.explanation: Quintessential Joey. The honesty of 'I just heard lunch' is perfectly economical character comedy. His complete lack of shame is the joke.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Hey Chandler, there's something I wanted to talk to you about. It might be a little awkward.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh God, is this about money? Because I can explain the $47 I spent on those imported candels for the wedding.

jokes.text: If you need money, it's a bad time. I'm buying 128 dinners tomorrow.
jokes.setup: Ross says he needs to talk about something awkward
jokes.punchline: Chandler immediately jumps to money anxiety, revealing his stress about the wedding cost with the specific detail of '128 dinners'
jokes.explanation: The specificity of '128 dinners' elevates this from a generic money joke. It's a sharp detail that grounds Chandler's anxiety in a real, relatable wedding cost panic.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Okay, I need to talk to you about something serious.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh God, what did I do?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: No, it's not about you. Well, it is, but... we need to define what we are.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Are we still friends?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yes, of course we're still friends.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Are we best friends?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yes, Chandler, we're best friends.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Are we best friends who occasionally make out?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What? No!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: But would you if I asked really nicely?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: We're not having this conversation.

jokes.text: I'm not gonna say this as your friend...but as Monica's older brother. / But you're still my friend? / Not for a few minutes. / Right now, are you still my best man? / No.
jokes.setup: Ross wants to deliver a serious brotherly warning and tries to separate his roles
jokes.punchline: Chandler keeps asking about the status of their friendship and his best man role, undercutting the gravity of the moment with bureaucratic precision
jokes.explanation: Very well structured exchange. Chandler's anxious need to categorize the relationship even during a threatening speech is true to character and funny on its own. The escalating clarifications build nicely.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: So if Monica and I switch roles, does that mean I have to start caring about thread count? Because I've been using the same sheets since 1997, and honestly, they've developed their own ecosystem at this point.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Chandler!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What? I'm just saying, if I'm going to be you now, I should probably know: is 800 thread count good, or is that like saying you have a mediocre personality?

jokes.text: Do I still call you Ross?
jokes.setup: Ross and Chandler have suspended their friendship temporarily so Ross can give a brotherly warning
jokes.punchline: Chandler, in peak anxiety mode, wonders if he even has permission to use Ross's first name during the suspension
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's funniest lines. The absurd literalism of worrying about what to call someone during a temporary friendship suspension is a perfect Chandler beat. Economical, surprising, and character-specific.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Did you just threaten me?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What? No! I was just... I was being protective!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: You literally said you'd 'break my legs if I hurt her.'

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Well, yeah, but I didn't mean it literally!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: That's the definition of literally.

jokes.text: Are we friends again? / Yeah. / You won't believe what Monica's brother just said to me!
jokes.setup: Ross just delivered his brotherly 'kick your ass' speech to Chandler
jokes.punchline: The moment they're friends again, Chandler immediately complains about what 'Monica's brother' did — not registering that Ross IS Monica's brother in this context
jokes.explanation: Sharp callback. The instant transition from 'friends again' to complaining about the same person playing both roles is a satisfying, well-timed structural gag.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Could I BE any more threatened?!

jokes.text: I'm responsible for all those. / I had to go with the odds.
jokes.setup: Monica lists things that could go wrong at the wedding: dresses not picked up, veil lost, no something blue
jokes.punchline: Phoebe casually confesses she is responsible for all three potential disasters, defending it as probabilistic logic
jokes.explanation: Classic Phoebe irresponsibility played deadpan. 'I had to go with the odds' is a great character-specific rationalization that gets a solid laugh.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: What if it rains? What if someone gets sick? What if the flowers don't arrive on time?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, I can help you with at least two of those things.

jokes.text: The commercial? / That play? / That other play? / The movie? / Yes! / The one about the dog who flies planes?
jokes.setup: Joey mentions he had an audition a while ago — everyone tries to guess which one
jokes.punchline: After multiple wrong guesses, Monica lands on 'the dog who flies planes,' implying Joey has had so many failed auditions it takes a whole list — with increasingly absurd options
jokes.explanation: Good escalating list structure. The absurdity of a 'dog who flies planes' movie and Joey's wounded 'that one hurt' sells it.

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: You know, back in my day we didn't have all these fancy special effects. When we made a war movie, we had to actually go to war.

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: That's right, I was there. Trenches, mud, the whole nine yards. Lost my best friend to a wayward shell.

jokes.text: Back then we called it 'The Great War.' / It really was.
jokes.setup: Joey is about to star in a WWI film
jokes.punchline: Ross pedantically notes that WWI was called 'The Great War' at the time; Joey genuinely agrees as if he were there, exposing his obliviousness
jokes.explanation: Very economical. Joey's earnest 'it really was' as if agreeing from personal memory is a sharp, quick gag that perfectly illustrates his cluelessness.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I got the part! I'm playing a soldier in World War One!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: That's great, Joe! So you'll be fighting the Germans?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No, no, the Germans were in World War Two.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, the Germans were in both wars.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Well, nobody told me that!

jokes.text: I'm off to fight the Nazis. / Wait, Joey. We fought the Nazis in WWII, not WWI. / Who was in WWI?
jokes.setup: Joey excitedly leaves for his WWI film set, announcing he's off to fight the Nazis
jokes.punchline: Ross corrects him; Joey's follow-up question reveals he genuinely does not know basic history
jokes.explanation: Joey's ignorance played straight and sincere. His follow-up 'Who was in WWI?' is genuinely funny because it's not a joke to him — he actually wants to know.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Actually, that's not what happened. Napoleon didn't—

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait, so you're saying I'm wrong?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yes, I'm saying you're... I mean... okay, fine, I don't actually know.

jokes.text: Who did we fight in WWI? / Mexico? / Yes. Very good.
jokes.setup: Joey still doesn't know who the US fought in WWI
jokes.punchline: He guesses Mexico; Ross sarcastically validates him to end the conversation
jokes.explanation: Ross's exhausted, sarcastic capitulation ('Yes. Very good.') is funnier than the guess itself. The callback to the WWI ignorance lands well and escalates the absurdity.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey Ross, I need to know who the enemies were in World War I for this audition.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Um, well... the Germans and the Austro-Hungarians.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Right, right. So basically just... the bad guys from Indiana Jones?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yes. Exactly. That's... that's correct.

jokes.text: Joey keeps touching his face in a scene. / I thought it might be a cool character thing. He's a face toucher.
jokes.setup: Joey is attempting to act opposite a serious (Oscar-caliber) actor and keeps touching his face
jokes.punchline: His excuse is that the character is simply 'a face toucher' — a completely made-up, unilateral character choice
jokes.explanation: Good cringe comedy. Joey confidently doubling down on an obviously wrong choice by naming it as a character trait is very much in his wheelhouse.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey, I'm a huge fan of your work. I've seen all your movies.

dialogue.speaker: Richard Crosby
dialogue.line: Thank you. That's very kind.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah, you were amazing in Die Hard.

dialogue.speaker: Richard Crosby
dialogue.line: I wasn't in Die Hard.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh right, right, sorry—Lethal Weapon.

dialogue.speaker: Richard Crosby
dialogue.line: No, I've never been in an action film.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Okay, okay, um... Breakfast at Tiffany's?

dialogue.speaker: Richard Crosby
dialogue.line: That was Audrey Hepburn. I'm a man.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Right, yeah, I knew that.

jokes.text: Here's a question you never want to ask: Can my dad borrow one of your pearl necklaces?
jokes.setup: Chandler comes in with a request from his cross-dressing father
jokes.punchline: The framing 'Here's a question you never want to ask' builds anticipation, then delivers the absurdly specific pearl necklace request
jokes.explanation: Well-constructed setup with the meta-framing device. Chandler warning us this is a bad question before asking it is a smart structural choice, and the specificity of 'pearl necklace' is funnier than a generic request would be.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I was preparing for my role! Method acting, okay? I had to understand what it felt like to be completely distracted and self-absorbed.

jokes.text: Did he say what kind of neckline he's wearing?
jokes.setup: Chandler asks if his dad can borrow a pearl necklace
jokes.punchline: Monica's response treats it as a perfectly normal fashion question — asking about the neckline to match the jewelry — normalizing the absurd situation
jokes.explanation: Monica's completely practical, fashion-forward response to an absurd situation is the funnier half of the joke. The deadpan normalization of a cross-dressing father-in-law is sharp writing.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Can I borrow some of your jewelry for my dad?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh my God, yes! Okay, um, let me see what I have. Do you want something classic? Or do you want to make more of a statement? Because I have this great chunky necklace that would really bring out his eyes.

jokes.text: Let me see if Rachel has anything. / Yes, include more people in this.
jokes.setup: Monica decides to involve Rachel in the necklace problem
jokes.punchline: Chandler's weary sarcasm ('Yes, include more people in this') perfectly captures his humiliation at his father's situation spreading
jokes.explanation: Solid deadpan callback. Chandler's resignation is funny but it's a lesser beat in the sequence.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I mean, the man wears a dress better than I do.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Yeah, he's got great gams.

jokes.text: Honestly, ever since we got engaged I've been waiting for something to flip you out. / Honestly? Me too.
jokes.setup: Monica and Chandler are having a tender pre-wedding moment
jokes.punchline: Chandler admits he's also been waiting for himself to freak out, undercutting the romance with self-awareness
jokes.explanation: Foreshadowing as joke — both characters know Chandler is a flight risk. His honest admission is both funny and character-revealing. Works better in retrospect given the episode's plot.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: We could ask more people about it.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh, great idea! Why don't we just take out an ad in the Times? 'Have you seen my jewelry? I'm an idiot.'

jokes.text: If you're calling before Saturday, you've reached Monica and Chandler. But if you're calling after Saturday, you've reached Mr. And Mrs. Bing. Please leave a message for... the Bings!
jokes.setup: We hear their answering machine message
jokes.punchline: The message is an overly elaborate conditional announcement climaxing in a joyful 'THE BINGS!' — Monica's controlling enthusiasm applied to a voicemail
jokes.explanation: Mildly amusing visual/audio gag about Monica's enthusiasm leaking into every detail. The 'the Bings!' crescendo is cute but not exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Tomorrow's our wedding day!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Yeah, I'm really looking forward to our date.

jokes.text: Mr. and Mrs. Bing! / We're the Bings!
jokes.setup: They greet Monica's cousin Maureen
jokes.punchline: Both spontaneously announce 'the Bings' with Monica's rehearsed gleeful delivery, echoing the answering machine
jokes.explanation: Callback to the answering machine. Monica's enthusiasm for the new name is consistent, but the joke is a lesser repeat of the previous beat.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Okay, so the napkins need to be pressed, the flowers need to be arranged by height, the seating chart needs to account for everyone's dietary restrictions AND their ability to make small talk, and—

jokes.text: Thanks for wearing... something.
jokes.setup: Chandler's flamboyant, low-cut-dress-wearing mother arrives at the rehearsal dinner
jokes.punchline: Her greeting to Chandler is a barely-veiled passive-aggressive acknowledgment of his outfit being minimally acceptable
jokes.explanation: Extremely economical. The pause ('Thanks for wearing... something') does enormous work. It's a perfect passive-aggressive mom joke in three words.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Hi, you've reached Monica and Chandler Bing.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: We're married!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: We're married!

dialogue.speaker: Both
dialogue.line: Leave a message for the Bings!

jokes.text: This is so exciting! I thought we screwed you up too much for this.
jokes.setup: Chandler's mom is excited about the wedding
jokes.punchline: She openly admits she thought her parenting had psychologically damaged Chandler enough to prevent marriage
jokes.explanation: Sharp dark comedy. The admission that his parents expected to have broken him is delivered with breezy parental pride — the tonal contrast makes it very funny. Very character-specific to the Bing family dynamic.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Everyone, this is my cousin Frank Jr.

dialogue.speaker: Frank Jr.
dialogue.line: Actually, I go by Erica now.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Wow, that's great. Congratulations.

dialogue.speaker: Erica
dialogue.line: Thanks. I'm still getting used to it.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, if you ever need any pointers, I've been a Chandler for my whole life.

jokes.text: I can't believe I'm going back to work to get spit on again.
jokes.setup: Joey mentions returning to the film set
jokes.punchline: The main thing he has to say about working with a great actor is the indignity of being spit on
jokes.explanation: Seeds the later spitting subplot. Mildly amusing, mostly setup for bigger payoff later.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Dad, you look great. I mean, it's nice to see you wearing clothes.

jokes.text: It's lovely to meet you. / Are you his mother or father?
jokes.setup: The Gellers meet Chandler's transgender/cross-dressing father Charles
jokes.punchline: Jack Geller, completely unfiltered, asks the deeply awkward question everyone is thinking
jokes.explanation: Cringe comedy from Jack's complete lack of filter. The joke lands on character, but the subject matter has aged somewhat awkwardly.

dialogue.speaker: Nora Bing
dialogue.line: I'm so excited about the wedding! I always thought Chandler would never find happiness. I thought we psychologically damaged him.

jokes.text: What? I've never seen one before.
jokes.setup: Judy scolds Jack for asking if Charles is a mother or father
jokes.punchline: Jack doubles down with complete sincerity, treating Charles as a genuine curiosity rather than being offensive
jokes.explanation: Jack's sincerity saves it slightly, but this is the weaker callback in the sequence. The joke structure is thin.

dialogue.speaker: Nora Bing
dialogue.line: I can't wait to have little Bings running around!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler Bing
dialogue.line: Yeah, well, given this family's issues, 'little Bings' sounds ominous.

jokes.text: Aren't you a little old to wear a dress like that? / Don't you have a little too much penis to wear a dress like that?
jokes.setup: Chandler's divorced parents come face to face at the rehearsal dinner
jokes.punchline: Charles's retort perfectly mirrors Nora's insult in structure but lands a devastating, anatomically specific counter
jokes.explanation: One of the best jokes in the episode. The parallel structure is pitch-perfect — Nora's ageist barb is a standard sitcom insult, but Charles's mirrored response ('too much penis') is unexpected, anatomically specific, and devastatingly economical. The structural symmetry elevates it from a one-liner to a mini comedic masterpiece. High quotability, strong rewatch value.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I can't believe I have to go back to work.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Do you know what I have to do? I have to go audition for a commercial where I play a guy who gets hemorrhoids.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: A GUY WHO GETS HEMORRHOIDS!

jokes.text: Of course you can kick his ass, son. You could kick anyone's ass you want to.
jokes.setup: Ross made his 'kick your ass' speech to Chandler and is now getting mockery for it
jokes.punchline: Jack, completely earnest, tries to reassure Ross that he could indeed kick ass — validating the absurdity of the whole situation
jokes.explanation: Jack's fatherly reassurance about fighting ability is a good callback but doesn't add much to the joke beyond repeating the premise.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: This guy just spit on me! He spit on me!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Well, look on the bright side - at least he noticed you.

jokes.text: Talk to Chandler's dad and keep him away from Chandler's mom. / But I don't know what he looks like. / He's the man in the black dress.
jokes.setup: Ross needs Rachel to manage Chandler's feuding parents
jokes.punchline: The identifying characteristic — 'the man in the black dress' — is delivered completely deadpan as if this is an ordinary description
jokes.explanation: Very economical. The deadpan delivery of 'the man in the black dress' as a matter-of-fact identifier is a great short joke that plays with the normalization of the absurd.

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: So... are you a man or a woman?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler Bing
dialogue.line: Dad, you can't just ask that!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler's Father
dialogue.line: It's okay, Chandler. I'm both.

jokes.text: 'A man, duh!'
jokes.setup: Rachel is introduced to 'Amanda,' the name Charles uses when dressed as a woman
jokes.punchline: Rachel immediately sounds out the name as 'A man, duh!' — a hidden pun in the name
jokes.explanation: Classic sitcom wordplay that actually works. The 'A man, duh' hidden in 'Amanda' is a satisfying pun with an extra layer of Rachel obliviousness to the person she just said it to.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Dad, you can't ask me that!

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: What? I'm just asking about your personal life.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: It's none of your business!

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: Well, when you think about it, it's really quite fascinating. If you look at the specimen from different angles, you can see how it all works together.

jokes.text: I'm Ross Geller. / Dr. Ross Geller. / Dad, please. As I was saying... I'm Dr. Ross Geller.
jokes.setup: Ross begins his best man toast
jokes.punchline: Jack interrupts to add the 'Dr.' title, and after scolding his dad, Ross immediately uses 'Dr.' himself, revealing he wanted it too
jokes.explanation: Perfect character-specific joke. Ross feigning annoyance at his dad's interruption and then immediately using the title himself is a brilliant character reveal — his ego is exactly as big as his dad's. Great structure with the false setup and self-betrayal.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I can't even pretend to handle this.

jokes.text: In fact, I think before he met Monica, the only real relationship he had was with a girl named Molly. And he would've married her, only she couldn't control her bladder. / It was his dog. Did I say it was his dog?
jokes.setup: Ross is giving a best man speech about Chandler's relationship history
jokes.punchline: The bladder issue sounds like a person problem until Ross reveals Molly was a dog — but the reveal is delivered with panicked, mid-sentence course correction
jokes.explanation: Good misdirection with the dog reveal. Ross's panicked 'Did I say it was his dog?' as he walks it back mid-speech adds extra cringe comedy on top of the punchline.

dialogue.speaker: Judy Geller
dialogue.line: You're not actually going to wear that, are you? At your age?

dialogue.speaker: Charles Bing
dialogue.line: Well, Judy, at least I'm not wearing something that screams 'I gave up on myself in 1987.'

jokes.text: Maybe I can wear the dress for Halloween!
jokes.setup: Monica laments that after tomorrow her wedding experience will be over
jokes.punchline: Her solution is to repurpose the wedding dress for Halloween — revealing how much she's invested in the fantasy
jokes.explanation: Mild Monica-specific character joke. Funny but not particularly inventive.

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: You know what, Ross? You're right. You're absolutely right. And anyone who says otherwise is an idiot.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Dad, that's... that's not really—

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: No, no, no. You could've handled it better? Please. You handled it perfectly. In fact, I think you showed remarkable restraint. If it were me, I would've punched them in the face.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You would've punched them in the face?

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: Right in the face. Multiple times. You're a better man than me, son.

jokes.text: Who will make sure nothing happens to it? / I'll do it. / Who wants it? Anybody? / I said I'll do it. / Nobody? / All right, I'll do it myself.
jokes.setup: Monica needs someone to look after her steaming dress
jokes.punchline: Despite Rachel repeatedly volunteering, Monica cycles through the same invitation as if she heard nothing — unable to trust anyone
jokes.explanation: Excellent Monica character comedy. Her compulsive inability to hear Rachel's offer because she's already decided no one is capable is very true to the character.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: How do I know which one is Chandler's dad?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: He's the one who looks like a woman.

jokes.text: And if I remember correctly, Ray-Ban was the official sponsor of WWI.
jokes.setup: Joey shows up to the wedding location wearing sunglasses to avoid being spit on during filming
jokes.punchline: Ross sarcastically 'validates' the anachronistic choice by claiming Ray-Ban sponsored WWI
jokes.explanation: Sharp callback that ties together two running gags. Ross's historically-absurd sarcasm is a good payoff and fits his character well.

dialogue.speaker: Charles
dialogue.line: Hi, I'm Amanda.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh, that's a cute name! A man-duh? That's so clever!

jokes.text: Maybe it's not what we think. Maybe it's: 'Tell Monica I'm sorry I drank the last of the milk.'
jokes.setup: Chandler has disappeared, leaving only the note 'Tell Monica I'm sorry'
jokes.punchline: Phoebe invents increasingly benign interpretations of the note
jokes.explanation: Good Phoebe optimism gag. The specificity of 'drank the last of the milk' is better than a generic example would be.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I'd like to propose a toast to the happy couple.

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: We already did that.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I'd like to propose a toast to the happy couple.

jokes.text: Or 'Tell Monica I'm sorry I used her tweezers to pluck my nose hair.' / He does that. I've seen him.
jokes.setup: Phoebe is generating alternative explanations for Chandler's note
jokes.punchline: Rachel's straight-faced confirmation that she has personally witnessed Chandler's nose-hair tweezer theft adds a dose of credibility to the absurd scenario
jokes.explanation: Rachel's unexpected corroboration is the funnier half. The deadpan 'He does that. I've seen him.' escalates Phoebe's absurdist riff into something more.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: So Chandler was in this relationship, right? And things were getting pretty serious. He was doing all these romantic things, staying up late, being super attentive...

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Turns out it was a dog.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I mean, not literally. Chandler wasn't dating a dog. The dog was just... there was a dog involved somehow. This came out wrong.

jokes.text: Or maybe he was writing to tell her that he's changed his name: 'Tell Monica I'm Sorry.'
jokes.setup: The chain of benign explanations for the note
jokes.punchline: Phoebe suggests Chandler changed his name to 'Sorry' — treating the word as a proper noun
jokes.explanation: The best of the alternative note interpretations. Treating 'Sorry' as a name is a genuinely absurdist and unexpected leap — classic Phoebe logic that feels surprising even in a string of similar jokes.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I can't believe the wedding will be over so fast. All this planning, and it'll be done in one day.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You know what? I'm going to wear this dress again. I'm going to get a lot of use out of it.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'll wear it to restaurants, to the movies... I mean, it's a beautiful dress.

jokes.text: Good God, isn't it possible that 'Sorry' is sitting in there right now?
jokes.setup: Ross insists Chandler has run away
jokes.punchline: Phoebe doubles down on the 'Sorry' name theory, pictured as a person sitting in the apartment
jokes.explanation: Good callback that extends the name joke with Phoebe's visual imagining of 'Sorry' as a person. The 'Good God' adds comic indignation.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I can steam your dress! I'm really good at steaming things.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's okay, I'll just do it myself.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: No, seriously, I can do it. I steam things all the time.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I appreciate it, but I've got it.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Monica, just let me help you steam your dress!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No, thank you.

jokes.text: If you don't find him and bring him back... I am gonna hunt you down and kick your ass!
jokes.setup: Ross is about to search for the missing Chandler
jokes.punchline: Phoebe invokes the same 'hunt you down and kick your ass' speech Ross gave Chandler earlier — turning the brotherly warning into a running gag
jokes.explanation: Smart running gag callback. The speech being recycled by Phoebe gives it new life and the diminutive-Phoebe-threatening-Ross visual makes it funnier.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Thank you so much for helping my grandmother today. She really appreciated it.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I have no idea what you're talking about.

jokes.text: I just hope that someday you guys find someone like Chandler. / I hope we find someone exactly like Chandler and soon.
jokes.setup: Monica is gushing about how lucky she is to have Chandler while Rachel and Phoebe know he's missing
jokes.punchline: Rachel's 'exactly like Chandler and soon' has a double meaning — she's also urgently hoping Chandler returns
jokes.explanation: Good dramatic irony joke. The audience knows Rachel means 'we need Chandler himself to show up.' The layered meaning is well-constructed.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: What? I'm wearing these because back in 1987, there was a huge spit epidemic. People were just spitting everywhere. It was crazy. So the government issued these sunglasses to everyone to protect their eyes. It's historical fact.

jokes.text: I know you're great and play all those Shakespeare guys... but you're spitting all over me, man.
jokes.setup: Joey is trying to give acting notes to his more accomplished co-star
jokes.punchline: Joey, the lesser actor, confronting a legend about spitting — his complaint is valid but the power dynamic makes it painfully awkward
jokes.explanation: Good cringe setup for the spitting escalation. Joey's 'you great Shakespeare guys' as a prefix to a spit complaint is funny.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God, he left! He just... he just left!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Wait, maybe he didn't leave leave. Maybe he just went to the store. You know, for milk or... or a mop, because our floors are really dirty.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Or maybe he had to go to the dentist! Yeah, he's been having this really bad tooth problem. Like, really bad. His gums are all swollen and he's been having like, this thick discharge—

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Or! Or he could've just gone to the bathroom and gotten stuck on the toilet like that one time, remember? His stomach was making all these sounds...

jokes.text: That's what real actors do. Enunciation is the mark of a good actor. And when you enunciate, you spit!
jokes.setup: Joey confronts the veteran actor about spitting
jokes.punchline: The actor defends it as a hallmark of good acting — reframing spitting as craft with a confident lecture
jokes.explanation: The pompous actor turning spitting into a philosophy of craft is a great absurdist escalation. The confident delivery of 'when you enunciate, you spit!' is quotable.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Maybe the note isn't an apology at all. Maybe 'Sorry' is a person's name. Like, 'Sorry called, he wants his jacket back.'

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That doesn't make any sense.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, maybe Sorry is from another dimension where names are apologies!

jokes.text: Have you seen Chandler? / No, I haven't. / He's getting married tomorrow, right? / Yes. Don't worry. Everything's fine. / We'll see you tomorrow at the wedding. / I wasn't invited. / Then we'll see you the day after tomorrow.
jokes.setup: Ross asks Gunther if he's seen Chandler, and after saying not to worry, mentions the wedding
jokes.punchline: Gunther reveals he wasn't invited; Ross's completely unempathetic response is to push the meeting date back a day
jokes.explanation: Excellent Gunther joke. His barely-acknowledged rejection from the wedding, and Ross's complete obliviousness in just adjusting the meeting time, is perfectly observed. The deadpan delivery of 'then we'll see you the day after tomorrow' is the kind of casual cruelty that gets huge laughs.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, you can dismiss it all you want, but I'm telling you, people change their names when they want to start fresh. It's a fact.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Phoebe, that's not how names work.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh really? Well then explain Sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Sorry. He used to be called Mad, but he changed it when he wanted to apologize for everything.

jokes.text: I see why the girls like coming here. / Why? / The sexy blond behind the counter.
jokes.setup: Jack and Judy have come to Central Perk; Jack says he sees the appeal
jokes.punchline: The 'appeal' is Gunther, whom Jack finds attractive — blindsiding Ross
jokes.explanation: Good misdirection — we expect Jack to reference the coffee or ambiance; instead it's Gunther. Jack's attraction to Gunther is a fun character note.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: If you don't find Chandler, I'm going to break your legs.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's not funny.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh, come on. You said it to me!

jokes.text: Gunther? / She just added him to her list.
jokes.setup: Jack just said he finds Gunther attractive
jokes.punchline: Phoebe casually reports that Judy has added Gunther to her 'list' of people she's allowed to sleep with — making Jack's attraction a couple's mutual activity
jokes.explanation: Good extension of the previous joke. The 'list' implies the Gellers have an open marriage arrangement, which is an absurdist detail that gets funnier the more you think about it.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Chandler is just so wonderful, isn't he? He's thoughtful, he's funny, he's so caring...

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Yes. Absolutely. The best.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Really great. Really, really great.

jokes.text: And if you see Rita Moreno, let her know I'm looking for her.
jokes.setup: Jack has just been told about the 'list'
jokes.punchline: Jack's equal-opportunity celebrity crush on Rita Moreno as his list candidate, volunteered casually, is the perfect mirror joke
jokes.explanation: Rita Moreno is a funny specific choice — not an obvious celebrity, which makes it more absurdist. The casualness of 'let her know I'm looking for her' as if she might walk in any moment is well-played.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Could you lower your script a little bit?

dialogue.speaker: Richard Crosby
dialogue.line: No.

jokes.text: Tomorrow's call sheet. / I'm not working tomorrow. / You are now. / No, you gotta get me out of it. I have plans. Important plans!
jokes.setup: Joey tries to get out of working tomorrow — the day of his friends' wedding
jokes.punchline: His vague 'important plans' has massive stakes the audience knows about but the director doesn't
jokes.explanation: Setup joke for the minister subplot. Functional but not particularly clever on its own.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I don't understand why he keeps spitting on me during scenes.

dialogue.speaker: Richard
dialogue.line: Well, it's called method acting, Joey. Real passion, real emotion—sometimes that involves a little saliva. The great actors of our time, they understood that spitting is an essential tool of the craft.

jokes.text: Oh, that's gone too. This is Monica's bathroom, right?
jokes.setup: Rachel goes to get toilet paper from Monica's bathroom, only to find it's been used up
jokes.punchline: The absence of toilet paper is immediately explained by confirming it's Monica's hyper-organized/controlled bathroom
jokes.explanation: The joke works because confirming it's Monica's bathroom explains everything — she'd have maximally used every resource. Quick and character-specific.

dialogue.speaker: Gunther
dialogue.line: I wasn't invited to the wedding.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Well, um... I mean, we wanted to keep it small, you know? Just family and close friends.

jokes.text: Oh, my God. / What? / There was a pregnancy test in the garbage. And it's positive. / Monica's pregnant.
jokes.setup: Phoebe and Rachel are crying in Monica's bathroom about Chandler's disappearance
jokes.punchline: In the middle of the marital disaster, they find a positive pregnancy test — adding a catastrophic new dimension to the worst-case scenario
jokes.explanation: Major plot bomb delivered as comedic escalation. The timing — discovered while crying in the bathroom about the missing groom — is perfect. The escalation from 'bad' to 'catastrophically worse' is excellent sitcom structure.

dialogue.speaker: Judy Geller
dialogue.line: Who is that sexy blonde behind the counter?

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: That's our son.

dialogue.speaker: Judy Geller
dialogue.line: Oh my God!

jokes.text: So I guess she won't be totally alone.
jokes.setup: They've just discovered Monica might be pregnant AND her groom has fled
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's silver lining is that Monica will have the baby for company when Chandler doesn't show
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best jokes. The economic deadpan of 'so I guess she won't be totally alone' — delivered as genuine optimistic consolation — is both hilarious and deeply dark. The specificity of the construction (perfectly minimal words for maximum impact) is excellent craft. Character-perfect Phoebe.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Mom, Dad, I need you to keep an eye on Chandler for me while I'm gone.

dialogue.speaker: Jack Geller
dialogue.line: Why? What's wrong with Chandler?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Nothing's wrong with him. I just... I have a feeling something might happen.

dialogue.speaker: Judy Geller
dialogue.line: Like what?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I don't know. Just make sure he doesn't do anything stupid. And if he mentions my list, tell him Jennifer Aniston is still at the top.

jokes.text: Oh, my God! / I know. Monica's gonna have a baby! / Can this count as her 'something new'?
jokes.setup: They've processed the pregnancy revelation
jokes.punchline: Phoebe applies wedding tradition logic — 'something new' — to Monica's pregnancy, suggesting it fills that slot
jokes.explanation: Brilliant Phoebe logic. Applying 'something new' wedding tradition to an unexpected pregnancy is the kind of lateral thinking that makes Phoebe jokes work at their best. Very economical and genuinely surprising.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Thanks, that was really intense!

dialogue.speaker: Richard
dialogue.line: Yeah, you really got me worked up there.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I could tell. You were spitting all over the place.

dialogue.speaker: Richard
dialogue.line: Oh, sorry about that.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Are you kidding? That's the highest compliment! When an actor makes you so emotional you can't control your saliva, that's when you know you're doing something right.

jokes.text: Hey, wait. Do you know what kind of birth control she uses? / No. Why? / Just for the future. This is hardly a commercial for it.
jokes.setup: Phoebe and Rachel pledge to keep the pregnancy secret
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's immediate pivot to researching Monica's failed birth control method — for self-preservation reasons
jokes.explanation: 'This is hardly a commercial for it' is a great line. Phoebe's self-interested follow-up after vowing secrecy is funny and the phrasing is sharp.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, wait. You don't understand. I can't come in tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I have... I have this thing.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No, no, no, it's not just a thing. It's a really important thing.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm serious! I have plans. Big plans.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Can't you get someone else? Anyone else?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Please, please, please. You have to believe me. This is huge!

jokes.text: I talked to Chandler's parents again. / You said he was missing? / No. I made it seem like I called to chat. Pretty sure they both think I'm interested in them.
jokes.setup: Ross is reporting his search activities while trying to keep Chandler's disappearance secret from his parents
jokes.punchline: His cover was so vague that both of Chandler's parents now think Ross is romantically interested in them individually
jokes.explanation: Good Ross incompetence joke. The implication that he accidentally flirted with both a flashy woman AND her cross-dressing ex-husband is a great absurdist detail.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm getting married today! I'm getting married today!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: My hair is perfect, my dress is perfect, everything is perfect!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Ooh, my back! Ow, my neck! But WHO CARES?! I'm getting married!

jokes.text: No, you don't! / Okay. But I don't suck!
jokes.setup: Ross claims documented night blindness
jokes.punchline: Phoebe immediately calls it out as a lie; Ross immediately concedes but defends only the 'I don't suck' half
jokes.explanation: Good quick exchange. Ross's immediate abandonment of the lie but insistence on his competence is a funny two-beat.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You know, Monica, you're like a little tiny person running around with a clipboard, and you have no idea what's actually happening around you.

jokes.text: I'm never gonna get married!
jokes.setup: Rachel is supposed to stall Monica; she claims to be in emotional distress to buy time
jokes.punchline: Rachel's self-pity spiral as a stalling tactic while Monica's actual wedding crumbles is comically self-centered
jokes.explanation: Mildly funny Rachel self-centeredness deployed as a plot device. Works in context but isn't exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh my god, what if I say something stupid at this interview?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Then I won't get the job. Then I can't pay my rent. Then I'll be evicted.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'll end up living on the street. In the cold. Alone.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'll develop a mysterious illness. No one will recognize me. I'll fade away into nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Or you could just, like, do well at the interview.

jokes.text: Maybe I should just forget about it. Become a lesbian or something.
jokes.setup: Rachel is lamenting her inability to find a husband as a stall tactic
jokes.punchline: Her proposed solution — casually 'become a lesbian or something' — is delivered as a logical career pivot
jokes.explanation: Mildly funny but the 'or something' is doing the most work — the vagueness of it. The joke itself is fairly generic.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Phoebe, do you have any tissues? I can't find any in my apartment.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, I think I have some in my bag.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh my God, Phoebe... is this a pregnancy test?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh! Yeah, that's mine. I was wondering where that went.

jokes.text: Any woman would be lucky to have you.
jokes.setup: Rachel floats the idea of becoming a lesbian
jokes.punchline: Monica's earnest, supportive response affirms the lesbian path without hesitation, applying it literally
jokes.explanation: Monica's supportive sincerity is the punchline — she hears the lesbian idea and just confirms Rachel would be great at it. Good economy.

jokes.text: Maybe I'd feel better if I slept with Joey.
jokes.setup: Rachel has exhausted the lesbian idea as a stalling tactic
jokes.punchline: Joey as emotional support/solution is a casually absurd suggestion that reveals the stalling has gone off the rails
jokes.explanation: Mild joke. It works as an escalation of Rachel's desperation but isn't particularly well-crafted.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh, but look on the bright side — you're gonna have a baby!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Phoebe, that's not the bright side.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: No, no, no — you'll have a baby to love, and it'll love you back unconditionally, and you'll never be alone.

jokes.text: It's not like it's your wedding. / It is my wedding. / Did I not make that clear? / You said your best friend is getting married. / Yeah, to me. / Yeah, I'm marrying my best friend. Isn't that beautiful?
jokes.setup: Joey tries to get released from set by citing his friend's wedding
jokes.punchline: He claims he's the one getting married, creating an ever-more-elaborate lie that he delivers as a beautiful romantic sentiment
jokes.explanation: Excellent Joey improvised lie. The escalating logic — 'my best friend is getting married, yeah to me, I'm marrying my best friend, isn't that beautiful?' — is a great comedic spiral. Joey's sincerity in selling the increasingly absurd story is pitch-perfect.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm pregnant!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God! That's amazing! You're doing the thing!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: What thing?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue... and something that stretches!

jokes.text: I'm sorry, Joey. It's still no. / I'm having surgery. / What? / I made up the stuff about the wedding because I didn't want you to worry. But I'm having surgery today.
jokes.setup: Wedding excuse fails; Joey immediately pivots to a new lie
jokes.punchline: Abandoning the wedding lie completely and replacing it with a surgery lie — delivered with the same sincerity
jokes.explanation: Good escalating lie. Joey's immediate pivot and the faux-concern of 'I didn't want you to worry' is funny. Sets up the great escalation that follows.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I can't believe this is happening. The flowers are dead, the caterer canceled, and I'm still holding this pregnancy test!

jokes.text: What kind of surgery? / Transplant. / But you're supposed to work on Monday. / Hair transplant. / But you're not bald. / It's not on my head.
jokes.setup: Joey claims to need surgery
jokes.punchline: Escalating questions force him to narrow down to a pubic hair transplant — through a chain of increasingly specific, backed-into-a-corner claims
jokes.explanation: One of the best jokes in the episode. The escalating logic chain — transplant → hair transplant → not bald → not on my head — is structurally perfect. Each answer is forced by the previous question, making the destination feel both inevitable and completely surprising. The implication of the final answer is funnier than any explicit statement could be. Very high quotability and rewatch value.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: So what are you using for birth control?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: The pill.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh. Well, that's only like 99% effective.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's actually really good.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, but that 1%? That's just waiting to happen.

jokes.text: We are never gonna find him. He's one guy in a huge city. / Oh, my God. Is that him? / That is an old Chinese woman.
jokes.setup: Ross and Phoebe are searching for Chandler in New York City
jokes.punchline: Phoebe mistakes an old Chinese woman for Chandler, suggesting her search image is very vague
jokes.explanation: Classic Phoebe obliviousness. The gap between Chandler and 'an old Chinese woman' is funny. Quick and functional.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Hi, Mrs. Bing? This is Ross Geller, Chandler's friend. I was just calling to see how you were doing and... uh... just wanted to chat!

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.line: Oh, how sweet! Is everything alright with Chandler?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What? Oh, Chandler? Yeah, he's great! We were just... we were just hanging out and he said, 'You know what? You should call my mom.' He loves you so much.

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.line: He said that?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Absolutely. In fact, he's right here next to me and he wanted me to tell you... that he misses you and he's thinking about you constantly and—

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.line: Oh my God, put him on the phone!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: He... he can't talk right now.

jokes.text: He could be in disguise, you know. / You know what? You're right. You're absolutely right.
jokes.setup: Ross points out it was an old Chinese woman, not Chandler
jokes.punchline: Phoebe defends her mistake by suggesting disguise; Ross sarcastically capitulates — both revealing how desperate they are
jokes.explanation: Decent follow-up beat. Ross's exhausted sarcasm blurring into genuine agreement from desperation is a nice character note.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: You're terrible at searching! You couldn't find anything if your life depended on it.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's not true! I'm very good at searching. I search all the time. I searched for my keys for three hours yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: And did you find them?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: No, but that's only because someone moved them!

jokes.text: So this is your office. / How'd you guys find me? I knew I should've hid at the gym.
jokes.setup: They find Chandler hiding in an office, surprised they found him there
jokes.punchline: His regret is not about hiding, but about choosing the wrong hiding spot — the gym would have been better
jokes.explanation: Good Chandler moment. His sole regret being his hiding strategy rather than the act of hiding is very character-specific.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, wait. Before we go in there, I just need to tell you something. I've been thinking... what if I just completely changed my life? Like, what if I moved to Vermont and became a sheep farmer?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Rachel, what are you talking about?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No, hear me out! Or I could learn to yodel. I could be really good at yodeling. Or maybe I'll just live in a van. A really nice van. With curtains.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You're stalling.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I could become a mime! A silent mime who only communicates through interpretive dance and the occasional kazoo solo!

jokes.text: And using the Internet to try to prove that I'm related to Monica.
jokes.setup: Chandler explains what he's been doing in the office
jokes.punchline: He's been trying to find a blood relation to Monica to make the wedding impossible — an absurdly logical escape plan
jokes.explanation: Exceptional joke. Chandler researching whether he's related to Monica to get out of the wedding is the perfect expression of his anxiety combined with his absurdist 'logical' problem-solving. It's funny, character-perfect, and totally original. The specificity of 'using the Internet' grounds the absurdist plan in a mundane detail that makes it funnier.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'm telling you, I need this job! I'll do anything! I mean it — anything!

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.line: Well, that's... that's great enthusiasm, but—

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No, you don't understand. I will work weekends, holidays, I'll sleep under my desk, I'll be your desk! Just... please, I'm begging you.

jokes.text: Because if I go home, we're gonna become the Bings. I can't be the Bings. The Bings have horrible marriages.
jokes.setup: Chandler explains why he ran away
jokes.punchline: He's afraid of becoming 'the Bings' — the brand they've been cheerfully announcing all episode — now recontextualized as a horror
jokes.explanation: Excellent callback that recontextualizes 'the Bings' from cheerful self-branding to existential horror. The irony of them excitedly announcing 'THE BINGS!' earlier makes this land harder.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I can't come in today. I'm getting married.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What? To who?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: To you.

jokes.text: They yell, they fight, and they use the pool boy as a pawn in their sexual games.
jokes.setup: Chandler lists what's wrong with his parents' marriage
jokes.punchline: The list escalates to 'use the pool boy as a pawn in their sexual games' — a specific, disturbing detail delivered matter-of-factly
jokes.explanation: Very strong dark comedy. The specificity of 'pool boy as a pawn in their sexual games' — delivered deadpan as part of a matter-of-fact list — is a great dark escalation. The word 'pawn' is a particularly funny choice.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm thinking about getting a hair transplant.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Where?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Well, let's just say it's not for my head.

jokes.text: Have you ever put on a black dress and asked me up to your hotel room? / No. / Then you are neither of your parents.
jokes.setup: Chandler fears he's doomed to repeat his parents' dysfunctional patterns
jokes.punchline: Ross's test for whether Chandler is like his parents is hilariously specific to their unique qualities — the black dress and hotel room
jokes.explanation: Excellent callback that ties together both parents' defining characteristics into a single test. The logic is absurd but sound within the show's universe. Very economical and extremely character-specific.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Are you drunk?

dialogue.speaker: Richard
dialogue.line: No, I'm not drunk. Watch this.

dialogue.speaker: Richard
dialogue.line: I can walk in a straight line.

dialogue.speaker: Richard
dialogue.line: See? Perfectly sober.

jokes.text: Only Paul Newman can make marriage work. And I've met me. I am no Paul Newman. I don't race cars or make popcorn. None of my proceeds go to charity.
jokes.setup: Chandler uses Paul Newman as his standard for a successful husband
jokes.punchline: He rules himself out not for emotional reasons but for failing to match Paul Newman's specific side-ventures (racing, popcorn, charity)
jokes.explanation: One of the best jokes in the episode. The absurdist specificity of ruling himself out of marriage because he doesn't race cars or make popcorn — legitimate Paul Newman metrics — is genuine comic brilliance. 'None of my proceeds go to charity' is a perfect economy-of-language final beat. High quotability.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh my God, is that Chandler?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's Phoebe.

jokes.text: Right now no one has a lower opinion of you than I do. But I totally believe you can do this.
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to give Chandler a pep talk
jokes.punchline: His motivational speech opens with an admission that he currently thinks Chandler is at rock bottom — before turning it into encouragement
jokes.explanation: Smart inversion of the pep talk formula. The admission of contempt before the encouragement is unexpected and very funny, while also feeling true to Ross's character.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Rachel, that doesn't make any sense.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No, I'm telling you, it totally does! You're just not listening!

jokes.text: Can you just come home and take a shower? / Well, yeah. But then... / We're just gonna go home and take a shower. That's not scary, right? / Depends on what you mean by 'we.'
jokes.setup: Ross breaks Chandler's paralysis by asking him to do just one small thing
jokes.punchline: Chandler's anxiety misreads 'we're going home to shower' as potentially involving a shared shower — his deflection via double entendre suggests he's coming back to himself
jokes.explanation: Good Chandler joke that also signals his recovery — when he starts making deflecting jokes, he's returning to his normal coping mechanism. The 'depends on what you mean by we' is well-timed.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm hiding at the gym. It's the one place no one would ever think to look for me.

jokes.text: All right! There he is! Good old Chandler with the homophobic jokes.
jokes.setup: Chandler makes a 'we in the shower' deflection joke
jokes.punchline: Ross's affectionate recognition of Chandler's return to form — identifying the specific Chandler comedy brand — is both meta and character-specific
jokes.explanation: Meta-self-referential moment that acknowledges Chandler's established comedy brand. Ross calling it out by name is a clever, slightly self-aware joke that gets a laugh while also serving the emotional arc.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What are you doing?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm looking for a way out of this marriage.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I could fake my own death, move to Yemen, become a goat herder...

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Actually, that doesn't sound so bad.

jokes.text: Who's Mike Smith? / I was sure this was my office.
jokes.setup: They're leaving the office where Chandler was hiding
jokes.punchline: Chandler discovers the office isn't even his — he hid in a stranger's workspace
jokes.explanation: Good callback punctuation to the hiding scene. Chandler not knowing whose office he was in adds an extra layer to his panic-induced stupidity.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Okay, here's the test. My father would never, ever do this.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: He'd never admit he was wrong.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, I'm not like that. I can admit when I'm wrong.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Okay, so you admit you were wrong about Monica and me?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: ...I'm like his father.

jokes.text: The nights are the hardest. / But then the day comes... and that's every bit as hard as the night. / Then the night comes again... / The days and nights are hard, I get it!
jokes.setup: Rachel is trying to stall Monica by commiserating about loneliness
jokes.punchline: Rachel's manufactured melancholy keeps cycling through the same observation; Monica's frustrated summary cut-off ('I get it!') is the punchline
jokes.explanation: Good escalation joke. Rachel's increasingly tautological melancholy builds to a natural cut-off that Monica provides. The structure is satisfying.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Only Paul Newman can make marriage work.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm not Paul Newman. I don't have his looks, I don't have his charm, I don't have his salad dressing empire.

jokes.text: Let's go to lunch! / I can't go to lunch! / Right. / Oh, good God, I've fallen down.
jokes.setup: Rachel desperately tries to stall Monica from getting ready
jokes.punchline: With no good ideas left, Rachel falls down — literally causing a physical distraction via slapstick
jokes.explanation: Physical comedy that works as a last resort. The delivery of 'Oh, good God, I've fallen down' as a dignified announcement of one's own slapstick moment is very funny.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Look, I'm not going to lie to you - you're not great at relationships. You sabotage everything.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: But you know what? You're one of my best friends, and if anyone can change, it's you. I believe in you.

jokes.text: We can't find Chandler's vest. / Found the vest. / We'll have to keep an eye on it, make sure we don't lose it again.
jokes.setup: Rachel was about to confess to Monica that Chandler is missing
jokes.punchline: She pivots to 'can't find Chandler's vest' mid-sentence; Ross immediately produces it and delivers an earnest note about vest-monitoring — selling the cover completely
jokes.explanation: Excellent comedic misdirection. The audience's tension is released in a double beat — the cover story itself is funny, but Ross immediately finding the vest and committing to 'vest monitoring' as a sincere mission is the real joke. The escalation from crisis to absurd micromanagement is very well-structured.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Hey, hey, hey! Why did you say 'go home'? Why not 'go to your place'?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What? It's just a figure of speech.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: No, no, no. You said 'go home and take a shower.' That implies we share a home. Are you saying we should move in together?

jokes.text: For a minute, I was like, 'Oh, my God! The worst has happened!'
jokes.setup: Monica was scared when Rachel started the 'we can't find Chandler's...' sentence
jokes.punchline: Monica's 'worst case scenario' was a missing vest — while the audience knows the actual worst case is happening — perfect dramatic irony
jokes.explanation: Strong dramatic irony joke. The audience's knowledge that the actual worst HAS happened makes Monica's relief at a mere vest situation extremely funny. Good structure.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Every joke you make is about you and Monica showering together.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, it's a very clean relationship.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's not helping your case.

jokes.text: Let's reset. / What?! He got me!
jokes.setup: Joey and Richard are filming the scene with real swords
jokes.punchline: Richard actually wounds Joey with the sword — confirming the spitting storyline's escalation into actual physical danger
jokes.explanation: Physical slapstick escalation. The indifferent 'let's reset' from the director while Joey has been stabbed is excellent.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I've been coming to this office for three months. I know everyone here, I have my own desk, my own computer...

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Wait a minute. This isn't my office.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I work two floors down.

jokes.text: Slippery little bugger!
jokes.setup: Richard Crosby, drunk, is trying to perform a sword fight scene
jokes.punchline: His commentary on the sword — 'slippery little bugger' — treats his drunken incompetence as a quirk of the prop
jokes.explanation: Good drunk acting moment. The pompous actor blaming the sword for his impairment is funny.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You know, time is just a construct that humans created to measure their own insignificance in the infinite cosmic dance of existence.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Okay, can we please just order the coffee?

jokes.text: So you two were married, huh? / What happened, you just drift apart?
jokes.setup: Ross is making conversation with Chandler's divorced parents
jokes.punchline: His obliviously banal 'just drift apart?' question to two people who clearly had an explosive, public divorce is clueless
jokes.explanation: Ross's social obliviousness is a reliable comedy vein. The euphemism 'drift apart' applied to what we know of the Bings is a good contrast joke.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: The wedding is at dusk.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Dusk? Dusk is my worst time of day.

jokes.text: Do you remember our wedding day? / Did you know I slept with the best man? / Yes, he told me. / At least I think that was what he said. / It was difficult to understand with his legs wrapped around my head.
jokes.setup: Chandler's parents reminisce about their wedding day in front of Ross
jokes.punchline: The anecdote escalates from 'I slept with the best man' to the vivid physical description of legs-around-head — oversharing in front of Ross with complete disregard
jokes.explanation: Excellent escalation joke. The layers — the cheating revelation, the casual confirmation, the vivid detail delivered as clarification — build perfectly. 'It was difficult to understand with his legs wrapped around my head' is an outrageously specific overshare that earns its shock. Great dark comedy.

jokes.text: I want to wear this every day. / You look so beautiful. / I'm so happy for me.
jokes.setup: Monica appears in her wedding dress
jokes.punchline: 'I'm so happy for me' — Monica's reflexive self-centeredness even in an ostensibly other-directed moment
jokes.explanation: Perfect Monica character joke. The slight correction from 'for you' to 'for me' is delivered as an unselfconscious slip that reveals everything about her character.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I lied. Chandler's vest is terrible.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What?!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I'm sorry, but it is. It's hideous. And I can't keep pretending anymore.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: But you said you loved it!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I know, and I'm sorry. But I was lying then too.

jokes.text: Did Chandler show up yet? / We got him back. Everything's fine. / Damn it!
jokes.setup: Rachel calls to check on Chandler's return
jokes.punchline: Gunther's 'Damn it!' upon hearing Chandler is back reveals he was secretly hoping the wedding would collapse so he could have Rachel
jokes.explanation: Brilliant Gunther joke. The 'Damn it!' is entirely unexpected and reveals volumes about Gunther in one word. Economical, character-perfect, and gets a big laugh. Classic unrequited-love-as-comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm just so relieved that whole vest thing is over. That was the worst!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: The worst? Monica, your apartment is on fire.

jokes.text: Joey, I have to go. / Don't hang up on me! I'll marry you and me right now! I have the power!
jokes.setup: Joey is desperate to officiate the wedding from the film set via phone
jokes.punchline: Joey offers to marry Rachel and himself, completely losing track of who is getting married — driven purely by his desperation to use his ministerial powers
jokes.explanation: Excellent Joey panic joke. 'I have the power!' is a perfect expression of Joey's excitement about his ordination, and offering to marry himself to Rachel in his desperation is a great absurdist escalation.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: You can't just show up drunk! What kind of professional does that?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: You gotta have standards, man. You gotta take this seriously.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, you just showed up an hour late smelling like a brewery.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: That's different! I was... networking!

jokes.text: Cover for me. / Maybe you're overreacting. You do that.
jokes.setup: Chandler says he needs fresh air and Ross is nervous he'll run again
jokes.punchline: Ross's attempt at reverse psychology — suggesting Chandler's flight instinct is 'overreacting' — is completely transparent and mildly insulting
jokes.explanation: Minor joke. Ross's transparent, failed reverse psychology is mildly amusing but not particularly well-crafted.

dialogue.speaker: Richard
dialogue.line: I dropped my sword! No, I dropped my sword! I dropped my sword!

jokes.text: Anastassakis Papasifakis wedding. Excellent.
jokes.setup: Ross is hunting through the hotel for a priest to perform the ceremony
jokes.punchline: His reading of a wedding board with an enormous Greek surname — delivered with 'excellent' as if it's a simple solution — is the joke
jokes.explanation: Mild comedy from the unpronounceable surname. The 'excellent' is funnier than the name alone.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: My dad was a drag queen. A Las Vegas drag queen. She wore a sequined dress, the whole thing. And she went by the name 'Helena Handbasket.' I mean, my mother was very theatrical, and my father was even more so. They had this very theatrical relationship, which was great... until it wasn't. One day he just left. Ran off with a jazz musician. And my mother... well, she got drunk. Very drunk. And that's when things got really weird. She started telling me things about their marriage that no child should ever hear. Like, graphic things. Physical things. She told me things about my father that I'm still trying to unsee. And now every time I hear the phrase 'passing time,' I have a minor panic attack. I need therapy. I'm pretty sure I need therapy.

jokes.text: I need you to perform another wedding. Can you do that? / I don't know. Are they Greek Orthodox? / Yeah. Yeah. / They're my friends, Monica Stephanopolis. / And Chandler Acidophilus.
jokes.setup: Ross tries to recruit the Greek Orthodox priest from another wedding
jokes.punchline: He invents Greek surnames on the spot — 'Stephanopolis' and 'Acidophilus' — the latter being a type of bacteria found in yogurt
jokes.explanation: Very funny absurdist joke. 'Acidophilus' as a Greek surname is a great specific choice — it sounds Greek-ish but is a probiotic bacteria, suggesting Ross grabbed the nearest Greek-sounding word he could think of. High rewatch value.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Thank you so much, everyone. You know, I have to say, this is the happiest day of my life. And it's all because of me. I mean, look at this dress. I picked it out. These flowers? I arranged them. This whole wedding? I planned every single detail. Chandler's just here because, well, he showed up.

jokes.text: He better not come here. He can't see the bride in her wedding dress. / As I recall, when we got married, I saw the groom in the wedding dress. / That was after the wedding. It's not bad luck then. / Honey, it isn't good luck.
jokes.setup: The Gellers discuss the bad luck of seeing the bride before the wedding
jokes.punchline: Jack references their wedding where the groom was in a dress — Chandler's dad — with Judy trying to claim the post-wedding timing makes it okay, and Jack deflating it
jokes.explanation: Good callback. Jack's correction — 'it isn't good luck' — is the best beat. The escalation from 'not bad luck' to 'also not good luck' is well-structured.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Wait, Chandler's back? I missed all the drama?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Yes, he came back this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: This is so typical! I go out for one coffee and miss everything. Was there yelling? Crying? Please tell me there was at least some yelling.

jokes.text: Are you okay? / Well, you're sweating. / Out of happiness for you and Chandler. These are beads of joy. / That's sweet. / Don't touch me.
jokes.setup: Phoebe is visibly stressed knowing Chandler is missing again; Monica notices
jokes.punchline: Phoebe calls her panic-sweat 'beads of joy' — then immediately breaks character by hissing 'don't touch me' when Monica reaches for her
jokes.explanation: Very funny two-beat joke. The elegant 'beads of joy' cover story followed immediately by the cracked 'don't touch me' reveals the paper-thin composure underneath. Great escalation and character work.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, wait! I am an ordained minister! I have the paper! I have the paper!

jokes.text: Aaron, you gotta let me go. The guy's hammered.
jokes.setup: Joey is trying to leave the film set for the wedding
jokes.punchline: Joey's reason for being released is the other actor's drunkenness — framed as a professional problem rather than personal need
jokes.explanation: Minor plot-progression joke. Functional but not particularly clever.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Excuse me, are there any other weddings at this hotel today?

dialogue.speaker: Hotel Staff
dialogue.line: Yes, there are three others.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Could you tell me their names?

dialogue.speaker: Hotel Staff
dialogue.line: Popadopoulos, Stefanopolis, and Xantipolous.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Oh, that's beautiful.

jokes.text: You wouldn't happen to have a very big fork?
jokes.setup: Joey needs to get the drunk actor to leave the set
jokes.punchline: His solution request — a 'very big fork' — implies he intends to physically prod or coerce the actor into leaving
jokes.explanation: Economical absurdist joke. The specificity of 'a very big fork' as a crowd-control tool is unexpected and very funny. The implication is vivid without being explained.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Father, I need you to officiate my wedding. My fiancée is Greek, and it would mean so much to have a Greek Orthodox ceremony.

dialogue.speaker: Priest
dialogue.line: What is your name, my son?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Uh... Yogurt... Geller. Ross Yogurt Geller.

dialogue.speaker: Priest
dialogue.line: That is not a Greek name.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Well, my father is... Starter Culture Geller. And my mother is... Lactobacillus Geller.

jokes.text: So I just talked to the director. That's it. We're done for the day. / We finished the scene? / You were wonderful. / As were you. / So I got your car. It's right outside. / Why? Are we done for the day? / That's what you told me. / Thank you. / You're welcome.
jokes.setup: Joey is trying to manipulate the drunk actor into leaving
jokes.punchline: Richard, too drunk to remember what he said, completely accepts Joey's lie and thanks him graciously in his actor's manner — while Joey cons him out the door
jokes.explanation: Good sustained cringe/manipulation comedy. The elegant mutual 'thank you / you're welcome' formal exchange while Joey tricks Richard out the door is a nice bit of controlled absurdity.

dialogue.speaker: Nora Bing
dialogue.line: It's not fortune, it's just a dress.

jokes.text: Is that my ass?
jokes.setup: Richard is being guided into a car
jokes.punchline: In his drunken state, Richard can't identify his own body parts as he's being loaded into the vehicle
jokes.explanation: Extremely economical drunk joke. Three words, delivered deadpan, that perfectly capture someone who is extremely intoxicated without overexplaining. High quotability.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'm not sweating, I'm glowing! It's happiness!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Ugh, get it off me!

jokes.text: You're not getting away this time, mister! Unless you want that ass-kicking we talked about!
jokes.setup: Ross spots Chandler outside the hotel and fears he's fleeing again
jokes.punchline: Ross invokes his 'kick your ass' speech again — the third iteration of the running gag — this time in a moment of genuine urgency
jokes.explanation: Third iteration of the running gag. Works well because the stakes are now real — Chandler is actually outside. The callback lands but is weaker than Phoebe's version.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, maybe if you didn't keep losing him, you'd know where he was.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: I don't keep losing him!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You lost him at the museum, you lost him at Central Perk, you lost him at the movie theater...

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Those were accidents!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: At what point does it stop being an accident and start being a cry for help?

jokes.text: I was. Then I went to the gift shop because I was out of cigarettes.
jokes.setup: Ross and Phoebe discover Chandler wasn't fleeing but was outside
jokes.punchline: Chandler's anxiety attack was interrupted by a mundane gift shop cigarette run, undercutting the drama
jokes.explanation: Good anticlimactic joke. The gift shop cigarettes as the mundane reason for being outside deflates the dramatic moment perfectly.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey, does anybody have a big stick or something? I need to knock Richard unconscious.

jokes.text: You obviously didn't see Chucky III.
jokes.setup: Chandler picks up a tiny baby onesie and says 'anything that can fit into this can't be scary'
jokes.punchline: Phoebe immediately cites Chucky III as a counterexample — a small doll that is terrifying
jokes.explanation: Excellent Phoebe line. The Chucky III reference is unexpected and very funny — it's a perfect logical counter to Chandler's baby onesie consolation. The specificity of the sequel number adds comic texture.

dialogue.speaker: Richard
dialogue.line: Am I dead? Is this the afterlife?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No, you just fainted.

dialogue.speaker: Richard
dialogue.line: But I saw myself lying there...

jokes.text: I've never walked down the aisle knowing it can't end in divorce.
jokes.setup: Ross is walking Monica down the aisle
jokes.punchline: His optimism is framed as relief that THIS marriage, unlike his own, cannot end in divorce — revealing his track record
jokes.explanation: One of the best jokes in the episode. It works on every level: it's character-specific (only Ross could say this), it's perfectly timed at a moment of genuine emotion, the economy is flawless, and it gets huge laughs while also being a little sad. The implication — that all his previous aisle-walks COULD end in divorce because he was the groom — is embedded in a single clause. Exceptional craft.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
