dialogue.line: I'm warning you, Chandler. I've been taking martial arts classes.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh yeah? Well I've been taking crazy classes, and I'm a lot further along than you are.

jokes.text: I wish your grandmother had lived to see this. / She's right there. / Not that old crone. My mother.
jokes.setup: Judy expresses a bittersweet wish about a grandmother
jokes.punchline: Jack corrects that the grandmother is present, then Judy clarifies she meant a different grandmother — calling the living one 'that old crone'
jokes.explanation: Good dark comedy. Judy's casual 'not that old crone' — said in front of the grandmother — is a sharp joke about elderly family friction. The structure of wishful → corrected → more-specific-and-darker is well-built.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Look at these tiny shoes. They're so small, they give me confidence. If a baby can wear these and still survive, I can wear a speedo.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's like saying you saw Child's Play and it made you want to buy a doll.

jokes.text: You look beautiful. / Is this new? / Not now.
jokes.setup: Ross compliments Monica; she asks about his outfit
jokes.punchline: His curt 'not now' in the middle of walking her down the aisle reveals he's checked out from the emotional moment into self-consciousness
jokes.explanation: Quick, economical joke. 'Not now' in this context is funny but it's a mild beat between bigger moments.

dialogue.speaker: Charles Bing
dialogue.line: Well, at least it's not permanent.

jokes.text: Who's this? / I'm Father Karabasos. / He's Greek Orthodox. / As are you.
jokes.setup: An unexpected priest appears at the wedding
jokes.punchline: Ross's confident 'as are you' to Chandler — asserting Chandler's Greek Orthodoxy based on Ross's earlier lie to recruit the priest
jokes.explanation: Good callback payoff to the Greek surnames scheme. 'As are you' delivered with full confidence to a confused Chandler is a great moment of Ross digging deeper into his lie.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I wish your grandmother could be here to see this.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Which one?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: The other one.

jokes.text: Dearly beloved... / That's my line! / I can take it from here. Thanks.
jokes.setup: Joey finally arrives as the Greek Orthodox priest also begins the ceremony
jokes.punchline: Joey's indignation at someone else starting with 'his' line, and his confident dismissal of a religious official, is a great comedy beat
jokes.explanation: Excellent Joey entrance. 'That's my line!' shows Joey treating ministerial duties as an acting role with blocking rights. His dismissal of an actual priest with 'I can take it from here, thanks' is very funny.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Your boutonniere is on backwards.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Could you *be* any more of a Monica right now?

jokes.text: You may be confused by this now... but you won't be Memorial Day weekend, 2002.
jokes.setup: Joey begins his speech as officiant, acknowledging his lateness
jokes.punchline: He reassures the confused guests that his reference to Memorial Day 2002 will make sense then — a wink to the future/audience
jokes.explanation: Smart meta joke. Joey's confident assertion that his bizarre situation will make sense on a specific future date is both character-specific (his confidence) and slightly meta-referential to the show.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey, hey, hey! I'm an actor. I know how this scene is supposed to go. And you're doing it wrong.

jokes.text: Let's get started before the groom takes off again.
jokes.setup: Joey begins the ceremony and wants to get moving
jokes.punchline: Joey casually references Chandler's earlier disappearance in front of all the wedding guests — blowing the cover
jokes.explanation: Joey obliviously outing Chandler's disappearance to the whole room in a single casual line is excellent. His complete unawareness of the reveal makes it funnier.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm sorry I'm late. I was at this audition, and it ran really long.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: But here's the thing - you're all gonna understand why I had to stay... in about eight to ten years.

jokes.text: Unless you don't want to.
jokes.setup: Monica finishes her vows — a beautiful, heartfelt speech ending with 'my friend'
jokes.punchline: After pouring her heart out, she nervously adds 'unless you don't want to' — revealing the insecurity beneath the speech
jokes.explanation: Brilliant joke that earns its laughs both emotionally and comedically. After the most beautiful vow speech, Monica's anxiety cracks through in those four words. The contrast between the poetry of the speech and the vulnerability of the postscript is perfectly calibrated. Very high quotability.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: We are gathered here today to join Chandler and Monica in holy matrimony. And Chandler, I just want to say, I really hope you show up.

jokes.text: Oh, wait. Do you take each other? / I do. / I do. / Yeah, you do!
jokes.setup: Joey pronounces them married, then realizes he forgot the vows
jokes.punchline: His hasty afterthought vow question, and enthusiastic 'yeah, you do!' as response, is entirely non-ceremonial but entirely Joey
jokes.explanation: Excellent Joey officiant joke. The marriage being completed before the vows, then backed up with an enthusiastic 'yeah, you do!' is the most Joey possible version of a wedding. The energy is infectious and character-perfect.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I, uh... I don't actually have anything prepared. I thought I'd just wing it.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: How hard can it be? I've been winging it my whole life!

jokes.text: Oh, crap. Okay. Let's do the rings.
jokes.setup: Joey has gotten the vows out of order and is trying to recover
jokes.punchline: 'Oh, crap' at a wedding is a perfect Joey ceremony fail
jokes.explanation: Very economical. 'Oh, crap' as a wedding utterance is funny purely for the inappropriateness. Joey's matter-of-fact recovery is good.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: He ran away? When? Why didn't anyone tell me?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Wait, never mind that—who's going to help me move this couch?

jokes.text: Once again... I pronounce you husband and wife. / Now kiss her again.
jokes.setup: Joey has to re-pronounce them husband and wife after sorting out the rings
jokes.punchline: 'Once again' and 'now kiss her again' — Joey treating his second pronouncement as a natural do-over with no ceremony
jokes.explanation: Good Joey callback. 'Once again' and 'now kiss her again' are funny in their breezy pragmatism about having done the ceremony wrong the first time.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I promise to love you, to cherish you, to stand by your side through thick and thin. You are my soulmate, my best friend, my everything. I vow to spend the rest of my life making you as happy as you make me.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: But if, for any reason, you turn out to be a serial killer, all bets are off.

jokes.text: I love you. And I know about the baby. / What baby? / Our baby. / We have a baby?
jokes.setup: Chandler declares his love and says he knows about the baby — implying the pregnancy test
jokes.punchline: Monica has no idea what he's talking about — she didn't take the test — leading to the revelation that someone else is pregnant
jokes.explanation: Excellent episode-closing comedic misdirection. The audience has known about the pregnancy all episode and assumed it was Monica's — the reversal in this final exchange is a perfect structural surprise. 'We have a baby?' is Monica at her most naturally funny. Great payoff to the whole B-plot.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Wait, wait, wait. Did I miss something? What happened?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You weren't paying attention during the vows!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No, no, I was totally paying attention! I heard the whole thing. Every word.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: You weren't even looking at the altar.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yes, I was! I was... it was very moving. Very moving ceremony. Couldn't have done it better myself.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You missed the part where they said 'I do.'

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I do! I totally heard that! I do! See? I got it!

tmdb_overview: So close to the wedding, Chandler suddenly realizes the overwhelming meaning of getting married and takes off without warning anyone. Meanwhile, Joey acts opposite a famous actor in a movie, but can't bring himself to tell him that he spits when he says his lines. Phoebe and Ross try to find Chandler before the wedding starts, while Rachel tries to hinder Monica, so that she doesn't find out the shocking news. On the day of the wedding Joey encounters a scheduling problem, while Phoebe and Rachel come across a surprising discovery.
insight: Wedding chaos drives 110 jokes across two hours—Friends' densest comedic output ever.
